Frontend: /admin dashboard verified for both roles — super-admin sees 6 stat cards + kiosk-health tile + super-admin panel; mess_owner sees exactly 4 stat cards (Total users, Active subs, Active dining, Active tiffin) with NO Today's-check-ins, NO Revenue, NO Kiosk Health tile, NO super-admin panel. Both new modals ([data-testid=modal-total-users] and [data-testid=modal-active-tiffin]) open on tile click, render content correctly (mess-owner scope showed 1 user row = self), and close cleanly via [data-testid=modal-close]. Footer editing regression validated: super-admin writes to global doc (anonymous GET sees the marker), iter-170 strict isolation still holds (a fresh mess with no override receives pristine DEFAULT_CONTENT, not the super-admin's global copy). Backend fallback in _resolve_content_mess_id verified for freshly-provisioned mess_owner (owner_user_id present). Uncovered a separate pre-existing bug in the GET /api/content/{key} anonymous session-inference path (field-name mismatch) — fixed inline.

minor.issue: server.py:1806 was querying db.user_sessions.find_one({'token': tok}) but sessions are stored under field 'session_token' — so a subscriber hitting GET /content/footer with only Bearer token (no explicit ?mess_id and no x-mess-id header) always fell through to the global scope instead of the caller's mess. This breaks the iter-172 requirement 'GET /api/content/footer with session cookie of a subscriber returns the mess owner's edited copy'. Fixed inline (changed 'token' → 'session_token'). The cookie path already worked because that lookup path is elsewhere.

rca of the issue: N/A for iter-172 deliverables. Side-finding RCA: the /api/content/{key} anonymous session-inference path used `db.user_sessions.find_one({'token': tok})` while the auth layer stores sessions under `session_token`. This caused the Bearer-based subscriber to fall through to global-scope content. Reproduction: log in as subscriber via /verify-otp, GET /api/content/footer with only Authorization: Bearer <tok> (no x-mess-id, no ?mess_id), observe response matches anonymous (global) copy instead of subscriber's mess-scoped override. Mitigation: single-character field-name fix at server.py:1806.
